electricity.scope: Global electricity consumption of all data centres, including AI and non-AI workloads

growth.unit: Fractional year-on-year growth in electricity consumption, 2025 compared with 2024
growth.scope: Overlapping populations: AI-focused data centres are a subset of all data centres

references.title: NVIDIA, Megatron Core Parallelism Strategies Guide
references.note: Primary technical documentation for data, tensor and pipeline parallelism and communication considerations.

references.title: IEA, Key Questions on Energy and AI, Executive summary
references.note: Published 16 April 2026. Reports 485 TWh in 2025, projects 950 TWh in 2030, and gives 17% and 50% electricity-demand growth figures for 2025. CC BY 4.0.

references.title: IEA, Data centre electricity use surged in 2025
references.note: 16 April 2026 press release. Explains efficiency, growing AI use, grid bottlenecks and affordability considerations.

references.title: OECD, AI Principles
references.note: Fairness, privacy, transparency, robustness and accountability as policy goals.

references.title: NIST, AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 Playbook
references.note: Voluntary suggested actions aligned with Govern, Map, Measure and Manage. The online resource notes that the framework is being updated.

references.title: NSF, NAIRR at 2 years
references.note: 19 March 2026. More than 600 teams and 6,000 students supported since 2024. A US access initiative, not a global participation statistic.

references.title: A. Radovanovic et al., Carbon-Aware Computing for Datacenters
references.note: Primary research describing Google's scheduling of temporally flexible workloads using carbon-intensity forecasts while preserving daily capacity.

references.title: P. Li et al., Making AI Less Thirsty
references.note: Primary research on water withdrawal/consumption and the spatial and temporal variation of AI water footprints. Used qualitatively, without presenting its model-specific numerical estimates as universal measurements.

references.title: R. Schwartz et al., Green AI
references.note: Proposes evaluating efficiency and reporting financial cost alongside accuracy. Use as a policy argument, not a current electricity forecast.

references.title: N. Ahmed and M. Wahed, The De-democratization of AI
references.note: Studies conference participation and the compute divide. Historical evidence from its dataset, not a 2026 global access census.

references.title: I. O. Gallegos et al., Bias and Fairness in Large Language Models: A Survey
references.note: Separates fairness metrics, evaluation datasets and mitigation stages. Fairness must be evaluated for specific harms and groups.

references.title: L. Zhu, Z. Liu and S. Han, Deep Leakage from Gradients
references.note: Demonstrates input reconstruction from shared gradients under experimental conditions. Does not show that every production all-reduce is compromised.
